title: Scott's father, family circumstances and the move to music
summary: His father came from Richmond in 1888, drove for a doctor, and wanted his son to be a doctor or lawyer, but Scott earned more as a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I'm the oldest, and after me came girls. And my mother, she was such a darling. How she made out and all like that -- my father, when he came to New York, he couldn't get any jobs. Colored men couldn't get jobs, because when the blizzard of 1888 --

Richmond, Virginia. And he was here when he was 20 years old, in 1888, he came to New York. And that blizzard so high, they didn't have the modern implements to clear a way, and it just stayed there til it melted. That's the way it was, then.

But he couldn't get any jobs outside of porters or janitor or what you call blue collar jobs. And -- but he loved horses, crazy about horses. He got a job with a white doctor, Dr. Thompson. And he drove for him, because in those days, doctors used to visit their patients. Of course, nowadays, you have to go to the doctor yourself. Doctors are scared to come out, they get mugged for dope, if they think they got dope.

But he drove the buggy for Dr. Thompson. Dr. Thompson was the doctor that brought me here. Yeah, old Dr. Thompson. And from then, he got those kind of jobs, because he didn't have a chance to get a real education, but he wanted his
children to get a good education. I was booked to be either a doctor or a lawyer, and I wound up being a musician.
How did they take that? Was there any -- as long as you brought the money home.

Well, I was making more in four nights playing than my father made all week. And I helped the family that way, those mouths -- every time a kid would come, it was a baby girl. And he wanted another boy so bad.
